samples.question: The picture shows exactly one solid pale-coloured patch on a white page. Every grey blob and every dark stroke lying outside that patch is background clutter and must be ignored. The patch is clearly longer in one direction than in the other; call that direction its long axis. Inside the patch there are many short dark strokes, all of the same length and thickness. Their individual directions differ from one another, so no single stroke settles the question, but taken together the strokes have one average direction; call that the grain. Take the angle between the grain and the long axis as the acute angle between those two directions, so that it lies between 0 and 90 degrees. The answer is along if that angle is less than 35 degrees, across if it is more than 55 degrees, and unclear if it is between 35 and 55 degrees. Does the grain inside the patch run along the patch's long axis, across it, or is it unclear?
